db_evidence.notes: episodes rows covering 73980-74160s (immediately after the 73976-73988s clue interval) explicitly describe 'white frost or smoke explosions', 'icy particle effects', 'ice-shard particle effects', and the boss 'shifts between an icy armored state and a more fleshy, roaring state'. topic_facts rows at 73980s and 74010s independently paraphrase the same content ('quadruped boss with pale spiked plating...frost/smoke explosions', 'boss shifts between icy armored state and fleshy roaring state'). This textual evidence alone is sufficient and unambiguous to answer 'Freeze', which is why 3 of 5 rollouts (00, 02, 04) answered correctly purely from semantic_search/run_sql without ever calling clip_qa, while the other 2 (01, 03) additionally used clip_qa for visual confirmation and got the same correct answer.

root_causes: N/A for failure — all 5 rollouts scored 5/5 on this question; there is no failure to diagnose.

Success driver: multiple independent captioning passes (episodes 3-min summaries and topic_facts one-line facts) both mention frost/ice/icy-particle effects at/after the clue interval, giving strong, redundant, easily-matched textual signal regardless of exact query wording.

The candidate answer set (Thunder Sting/Burn/Freeze/Poison) has only one term ('freeze'/'ice'/'frost') with clear lexical overlap to the DB captions, making retrieval robust to query phrasing variance across the 5 rollouts.
what_worked: Windowed run_sql queries (episodes/topic_facts/event_steps/object_states/visual_clips filtered by start_s or time_s BETWEEN ~73800 and ~74500) around the clue interval reliably surfaced the frost/ice captions in every rollout.
Semantic_search across multiple tables (episodes, topic_facts, entities, visual_clips) with varied English and Chinese query phrasings converged on the same ice/frost evidence.
Two rollouts used clip_qa as a confirmatory step even though text evidence was already sufficient, adding robustness without changing the (already-correct) outcome.
All 5 final answers correctly selected option 3 and gave a coherent justification (first phase = fire/burn, second phase adds freeze/ice) matching the reference answer '3'.
transferable_lessons: For 'which additional negative effect appears' style multiple-choice questions, a windowed run_sql over episodes/topic_facts around the clue interval is often sufficient — the boss-fight captions already lexicalize elemental effects (fire, frost, ice, poison) directly, so heavy semantic_search fan-out or clip_qa is not strictly required when captions are this explicit.

When db captions already contain unambiguous English descriptors (e.g. 'frost', 'icy particle effects') for one of the answer options, calling clip_qa is a low-risk confirmatory step but not necessary — agents that skipped it were not penalized.

Bilingual (English + Chinese) query variants are a reasonable belt-and-braces approach but in this case both languages found the same underlying English-captioned rows, since the memory DB captions are in English.
open_questions: None of the rollouts failed, so there is nothing to further diagnose for this question; open question is only whether this style of question (single option with unique visual/textual referent) is a fair test of the pipeline's failure modes given it appears trivially retrievable from text alone.
